text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- Editorial blames Albanian politicians for not reaching common view on new electoral law, saying the only solution for Prime Minister Bashkim Fino's government to overcome political deadlock is to ask for international help.

- U.S. Embassy in Tirana rejected local media allegations that deterioration of American-Albanian relations was due to President Sali Berisha's refusal to offer Sazan island to the American troops, making clear the island was considered as not available for military purposes.
- Situation in northern town of Shkoder is still tense.
- Local authorities in Vlore asked Italian troops to help them restore law in the town.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Socialists should disband the committees of public salvation in the south before the elections, Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu said after meeting Socialist leader Fatos Nano.
- Albanian army fell apart because of rebellion organised by former communist and secret police officers.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Some 27 people were killed, among them 12 children, when they triggered a blast while looting an underground military weapons store in Selize, near Tirana.
- A surgeon in Tepelena was beaten up by a family after failing to save the life of their relative.
- King Leka I blames the Pentagon for not backing his plan to overthrow Stalinist dictatorship of Enver Hoxha in 1979.
ALBANIA
- Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj should resign and be sent to a military court to be tried for the Burrel massacre in which 22 people were killed.
- Editorial claims Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano is a spokesman of the rebel committees in the south.
ZERI I POPULLIT

- God, save us from the President! paper says, adding that the Albanians almost lost their state, but not President Sali Berisha who it said is the key figure to be blamed for chaos, unrest and violence.
- Full page report on committees in the south, saying they have nothing to do with criminal gangs which terrorise people across the country.
- Vlore residents should be respected by all Albanians as they were the first to rise up against Berisha's government.
